projects.name: Labor planning model
projects.problem: Warehouse staffing in Arizona and Colorado was set by supervisor intuition, causing overtime on light days and dock congestion on peak days.
projects.what_i_did: Analyzed two years of inbound data in SQL to forecast volume by day, shift and zone. Built productivity benchmarks per position, turned them into a labor formula, and designed a Power BI planning dashboard for supervisors. Validated the model against history and with supervisor feedback.
projects.result: Published in Shamrock's Power BI environment as a production tool. Supervisors started using it right away, and leadership said it exceeded expectations.

projects.name: Driver bid optimization
projects.problem: Weekly driver schedules ("bids") were built by hand. Fewer, better bids mean lower labor cost and better driver retention in a tight labor market.
projects.what_i_did: Framed bid building as a constrained optimization problem with DOT rest rules, weekly hour limits, license classes and days off. Cross-checked planned against GPS-tracked route times to set safe buffers, then built a greedy heuristic with a local search improvement step.
projects.result: Delivered a documented, repeatable framework and data pipeline for the transportation planning team. The team said the analysis exceeded expectations.

projects.name: Recall fee strategy
projects.problem: Were Shamrock's fees for product recalls and withdrawals covering the true cost, and being billed and collected consistently?
projects.what_i_did: In a team project, ran 30+ interviews across seven departments to map every recall activity. Built a fully loaded labor cost model for each fee and audited recent recall events to measure under-recovery and collection gaps.
projects.result: Presented to about 100 leaders, including the company president. Recommended new fee rates, an annual review cycle and a one-page fee scorecard, and leadership committed to implementing them.
